Coram: Honourable Mr. Justice Rajeev Ranjan Prasad
Oral Judgment

This writ application has been preferred for de- sealing of the factory (Mill) of the petitioner which has been sealed by police authorities alleging that the petitioner was involved in manufacturing of adulterated articles of food which will be an offence under the Food Safety and Standard Act, 2006.

For the purpose of release, at this stage, learned counsel representing the petitioner has raised an issue that the police authorities, in any case, are not empowered under the Code of Criminal Procedure to seal an immovable property, and in the present case, the sealing has been done only by making an Patna High Court Cr. WJC No.974 of 2018 dt.27-04-2018 2 allegation that the mustered oil and vegetable oil etc., which are being prepared in the factory, were adulterated.

A copy of judgment dated 26.05.2015 passed by a co-ordinate Bench of this court in Cr.W.J.C. No. 331/2015 (M/s Parmatma Allied Feed Co. Pvt. Ltd. Vs. The State of Bihar and others) has been placed before me to canvass that the learned co-ordinate Bench while hearing a similar kind of contention had taken a view that such seizure which was in the said case at the instance of Food Safety Officer was not just and proper and no such power was vested with the authority who had lodged the First Information Report and sealed the premises.

Learned counsel also submits that in the present case he is seeking only de-sealing of the factory (Mill) and not the goods against which there are allegations of being adulterated.
He however submits that he will be seeking release those goods as and when advised.

On the other hand, learned counsel representing the State submits that the police authorities had moved to seal the premises in question when a complaint was received that the petitioner was involved in manufacturing of adulterated oil and as such it is a bona fide action taken by the police authorities.

It is also submitted that samples have been sent for examination Patna High Court Cr.
WJC No.974 of 2018 dt.27-04-2018 3 and the results are awaited.

Having heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned counsel representing the State, at this stage, considering that the petitioner is only seeking de-sealing of the factory (Mill), this court would direct respondent Nos. 3 & 4 namely, Superintendent of Police, Kaimur at Bhabua and the Officer-in- Charge, Durgawati Police Station, Kaimur at Bhabua respectively to provisionally de-seal the factory premises of the petitioner within a period of one week from the date of his furnishing two sureties to the satisfaction of learned court below.

The seized oil shall be kept separately and the factory premises shall be handed over to the petitioner subject to the terms and conditions that he will abide by the final result of the case, and during pendency of the case, he would not transfer the property in question to any other person.
With the aforesaid direction, this writ application stands disposed off.

(Rajeev Ranjan Prasad, J.) Rajeev/-
